correctness.rationale: All circuits of the rank-two dual are complements of nonloop parallel classes and match all nonempty neighborhoods; direct circuit forcing proves equality of closure on every subset. For uniqueness, additive component forcing plus DeAlba Theorem 3.3 leaves exactly one multipartite nontrivial component; the dual matroid determines its vertices and edges. The enumerator, exchange graph and Tutte formula follow from bases and rank partition; finite checks corroborate 232 cases but are not used as infinite proof.

evidence: Known: connected G has Z-minus(G)=|V(G)|-2 iff G is complete multipartite (DeAlba 2014).
Known: complete bipartite graphs give SZF matroids (Cooper–Fickes 2023); uniform corank-two matroids are SZF-realizable (Hall–Pfeil–Taylor 2026).
New: arbitrary looped rank-two duals are uniquely encoded by isolated vertices and multipartition classes; their circuit families equal graph neighborhoods.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A rank count does not recover the closure lattice or unique realizing graph. The proof combines the known scalar converse with a new explicit identification of all dual circuits as neighborhoods, and recovers every parallel class from the induced matroid. This yields universal corank-two existence and labelled uniqueness beyond the cited restricted results.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies a natural stratum of the general SZF-realizability problem: every labelled corank-two matroid is realizable by exactly one simple graph, including every nonuniform parallel-class pattern and any loops of its dual. This is more than a known forcing-number computation: it identifies the full closure matroid, supplies the inverse graph reconstruction and complete Tutte and minimum-set enumerators.
